what is a vision transformer (vit)

a vision transformer (ViT) splits input into a sequence of tokens, prepends a learnable [CLS] token, adds positional embeddings, and processes them through stacked transformer blocks of multi-head self-attention and MLP layers. The [CLS] token output is used for classification.
explain universal vit code

the UniversalViT model is a generic transformer classifier. It (1) projects input tokens of shape (B, N, input_dim) to embed_dim with a Linear layer, (2) prepends a learnable cls_token, (3) adds positional embeddings, (4) runs them through `depth` TransformerBlocks (each = LayerNorm -> MultiHeadAttention -> residual -> LayerNorm -> MLP -> residual), (5) takes the cls token, and (6) maps it to num_classes via a Linear head.
how does multi head self attention work

multi-head self-attention projects the input to query, key, value vectors, splits them into `heads` parallel heads of size head_dim, computes scaled dot-product attention (softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V) per head, concatenates the heads, and projects back to the model dimension.
what is the cls token in vit

the [CLS] token is a learnable embedding prepended to the input sequence. After all transformer layers, its final hidden state is used as an aggregate representation of the whole sequence for classification.
why add positional embeddings in transformers
self-attention is permutation-invariant, so positional embeddings inject order information by adding a learnable or sinusoidal vector to each token embedding.
how to train universal vit step by step

1) build the model with input_dim/seq_len/num_classes, 2) move to device, 3) create AdamW optimizer and CrossEntropyLoss, 4) for each step: zero_grad, forward pass logits = model(x), compute loss = criterion(logits, y), loss.backward(), optimizer.step().
what does mlp_ratio mean in transformer
mlp_ratio is the multiplier for the hidden dimension of the feed-forward MLP inside each transformer block. With dim=256 and mlp_ratio=4 the hidden layer has 1024 units.
why use layernorm in transformer blocks
LayerNorm stabilizes training by normalizing activations across the feature dimension. ViT uses pre-norm (LayerNorm before attention/MLP) which improves gradient flow in deep transformers.
can vit be used for text audio and tabular data

yes — any data that can be expressed as a sequence of feature vectors (B, N, D) can be fed into a ViT-style transformer. Text uses word/subword embeddings, audio uses spectrogram/MFCC frames, tabular data treats each row of features as tokens.
pytorch universal vit example code

```python
class UniversalViT(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, seq_len, num_classes, embed_dim=256, depth=6, heads=8, dropout=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_proj = nn.Linear(input_dim, embed_dim)
        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1,1,embed_dim))
        self.pos_embed = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, seq_len+1, embed_dim))
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([TransformerBlock(embed_dim, heads, dropout=dropout) for _ in range(depth)])
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        self.head = nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_classes)
    def forward(self, x):
        B = x.size(0)
        x = self.input_proj(x)
        cls = self.cls_token.expand(B,-1,-1)
        x = torch.cat([cls,x], dim=1) + self.pos_embed[:, :x.size(1)+0]
        for blk in self.blocks: x = blk(x)
        return self.head(self.norm(x)[:,0])
```
